source.title: A Unified Stability Analysis of SAM vs SGD: Role of Data Coherence and Emergence of Simplicity Bias

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices and checklist.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses generalization, simplicity bias, and stability, but does not measure held-out train–test gaps or test any listed claim version. Its experiments report stability, coherence, and feature-rank results instead.
record.gate_note: No result tests a listed version: there are no natural-label held-out errors, width sweeps, convolution-versus-fully-connected comparisons, optimizer generalization comparisons, dropout tests, magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons, or removals of memorized examples. The paper reports coherence, feature-rank, and convergence results; these are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives local dynamical-stability conditions and measures coherence, curvature, feature rank, and convergence. It reports no held-out performance comparisons testing V1–V8. Its equal-flatness constructions concern trace-based curvature and solution complexity, not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness and measured generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate as an account of the authors' interpretation. They argue that coherence governs local stability and that SAM strengthens a preference for simpler solutions, offering a proposed explanation of generalization. Their results establish stability and representation properties rather than measured generalization improvements. The empirical scope includes an additional CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 proxy experiment in Appendix A, beyond the main synthetic two-layer experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes local stability and coherence, with synthetic two-layer ReLU experiments; it does not reproduce the claim versions’ generalization-gap methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported coherence and feature-rank values vary with optimizer and SAM radius. The paper also reports that convergence boundaries shift with batch size, noise scale, and SAM radius, and that convergence speed varies with solution complexity C; these are stability results, not generalization-gap results.

fits_no_version.finding: After 200 epochs, CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 feature rank is 148.33 for SGD and 157.67, 144.33, and 128.67 for increasing SAM radii. Approximate coherence is respectively 1.0045, 1.0052, 1.0771, and 1.0907; reported uncertainties do not establish significance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer and SAM radius affect representation rank and approximate gradient coherence; these measurements alone do not establish changes in generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems and synthetic experiments relate local stability to coherence and show different stability or convergence behavior for constructed solutions with equal Hessian trace but different feature complexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local optimization stability can distinguish solutions that a trace-based flatness measure does not distinguish.

record.problems: The experiments do not report train–test error gaps. The authors state that their analysis uses a local linear approximation and that the empirical study is limited to two-layer ReLU networks and synthetic data in the main experiments. The CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 measurements use an approximate coherence measure on a fixed subset of 100 samples; Table 2 reports ± values without defining them in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No results relevant to the listed claim versions were omitted. Local convergence-boundary and convergence-speed results (Figure 1 and Appendix C.3–C.4) concern stability rather than generalization gaps and are not rows for these versions.

untested.parts: No comparison of random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural versus random labels.
No width sweep measuring test error beyond the width required for interpolation.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected held-out performance comparison or local-connectivity ablation.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out comparison under limited or broader tuning; SAM is not an Adam-style adaptive optimizer comparison.
Batch size is varied for local convergence boundaries, without held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No dropout intervention measuring held-out error.

No magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, measured generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based predictors. Equal trace-based flatness across constructed solutions does not test this version.
No influence-based memorization estimates followed by example removal, retraining, and test-accuracy comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The ± quantities in Table 2 are not defined. Main-text synthetic experiments report decreasing effective coherence with SAM, whereas Appendix A reports increasing approximate coherence at larger radii; the quantities and settings differ. Neither pattern warrants a verdict on V7. No omitted result tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test random-label memorization against natural-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep or test-error results.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or measured generalization-gap comparison.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining test.

relation.reason: It discusses memorization and flatness–generalization explanations, but reports no held-out comparisons testing the claim versions and does not operationally use their findings as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study measures dynamical stability, coherence, curvature and representation complexity; it does not test V1–V8. Equal-trace-flatness constructions do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of generalization gaps.
